subject: POC evaluation plan & success criteria — Acme (post-demo)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Meyers <jordan@acme.com>, Sam Patterson <spatterson@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC evaluation plan & success criteria — Acme (post-demo)

Hi Jordan & Sam,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciated the context and the product team’s clarity on their goals. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the proposed POC approach and next steps so we can align stakeholders and get a kickoff on the calendar.

High-level POC goal:
- Validate that Redwood Inference can meet Acme’s latency & cost targets while maintaining output quality for your in-app assistant.

Proposed success criteria (draft):
- Latency: p95 inference latency <= 300ms for 99% of requests in production-shaped traffic.
- Quality: automated offline eval score >= 0.88 on your rubric AND no critical production regressions in a 1-week online shadow (see eval methodology below).
- Cost: per-token inference cost not to exceed $0.0008 in expected steady-state config.
- Operational: model pins, autoscaling policy, and canary rollback validated in staging.

Evaluation plan (next two phases):
1) Offline evals (2 weeks)
   - Run your canonical prompt set + sampled production queries through candidate models.
   - Use grading rubric (accuracy, safety, hallucination rate, latency impact). We’ll provide a CSV template for graders.
2) Online shadow (1 week)
   - Shadow traffic routing (read-only) to measure latency under real traffic and capture skirt cases. No customer-facing outputs.
   - Manual spot-checks + automated regression alerts.

Ownership & stakeholders:
- Acme: Jordan (PM) — evaluation sign-off, Elena (VP Product) — exec approver, Sam (Eng) — data access and infra support.
- Redwood: Marissa (AE) — project lead & commercial; Dylan (SE) — technical lead.

Data & access needs:
- Sample prompt set + labels (CSV), and an S3 read-only bucket for the shadow run OR API tokens for a staging environment.
- Compliance: we’ll need to confirm retention settings and any masking requirements prior to shadow.

Next steps / asks:
1) Can you confirm the success criteria above or flag changes by EOD Thursday?
2) Share the canonical prompt set and a staging API endpoint or S3 access for Dylan to scope the shadow run.
3) Tentative kickoff: Wednesday 2027-05-26, 10:00am PT — does that work?

Attaching: redwood-poc-template.xlsx (POC timeline & responsibilities)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa — great write-up and aligns with what we discussed. A couple of quick notes from our side: 

- The latency target is aggressive but reasonable; we’ll validate with our production traffic distribution. If we see longer tail behavior we might need to adapt the p95 objective to p99 for specific flows.
- For quality, our Product team prefers a blended metric: 70% automated rubric + 30% human spot checks for edge cases. Can you include a sample rubric?
- Elena (VP Product) wants to be included in the kickoff — I’ve cc’ed her here (elena@acme.com).

On the shadow approach: we’re slightly concerned about any potential leakage even in read-only mode. Can you confirm what logs Redwood retains during a shadow run and whether we can enable additional masking? Sam, can you weigh in on infra access — do you want us to provide an S3 sample bucket or a staging endpoint?

We can confirm the checklist by Thursday EOD. Kickoff on Wed 5/26 at 10am PT works for us.

—Jordan
Jordan Meyers

Jordan — thanks, noted. I’ve updated the plan below to reflect the blended quality metric and to call out log retention/masking details. Attaching a short doc with a sample grading rubric and the POC responsibilities matrix.

Updated quality approach:
- Quality score = 0.7 * automated rubric score + 0.3 * human spot-check score.
- Automated rubric will measure correctness, instruction-following, and hallucination rate.
- Human spot checks (10–15 prompts/day during shadow) to validate edge cases.

Shadow run logs & retention:
- By default, Redwood stores request logs and model outputs for 30 days for debugging. For POCs we can:
   a) shorten retention to 7 days,
   b) redact PII fields via configurable masking rules, and
   c) support a read-only bucket export for anything you want to pull into your systems.

Masking & compliance:
- We’ll work with your security team to define masking rules prior to the shadow kickoff. Dylan will lead the technical conversation on required access patterns.

Attached: poc-success-criteria.docx (grading rubric + sample CSV for graders)

If that looks good, next actions:
- Jordan/Sam: share canonical prompt set and choose access method (S3 vs staging endpoint).
- Elena: confirm kickoff availability for 2027-05-26 10:00am PT.

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once we have confirmation.

Best,
Marissa

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: POC evaluation plan & success criteria — Acme (post-demo)

Hey all — quick technical clarifications from our side: 

1) Shadow architecture options:
   - Option A (recommended): Route a copy of production traffic to Redwood’s staging cluster via a secure VPN peering or mutually-authenticated TLS endpoint. This avoids live customer exposure and gives us real latency measurements.
   - Option B: S3 replay of sampled requests for an offline load test — good for early validation but won’t capture real queuing/latency at scale.

2) Data handling & retention:
   - Masking: we can apply regex/hierarchical PII rules before logs are persisted.
   - Retention: confirm 7-day retention for POC logs and we’ll enforce automatic deletion.

3) Grading rubric (ops notes):
   - We recommend at least 200 labeled prompts for the automated rubric to stabilize metrics.
   - For human spot checks during the 1-week shadow, we’ll suggest a stratified sample across endpoints and user flows.

4) Access requirements for shadow run:
   - Either provide a read-only S3 bucket with sample payloads + mapping file, or grant a staging API key scoped to read-only for shadow.

I’ll be available on the kickoff to pair on the initial infra test.

—Dylan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
